messages.subject: Re: Shiny app instantly "disconnected from server" as soon as app is deployed
parts:
Have you checked the logs for your application using the rsconnect::showLogs() function or looking in the shinyapps.io dashboard?

On Mon, Feb 15, 2016 at 12:54 PM, Jeremy Schwartzbord <jrs...@cornell.edu> wrote:
Hello,

I attempted to deploy my first shiny app with Shinyapps.io. Deployment was "completed" (see screenshot of RStudio ; however, as soon as the app loads, a window pops up stating "Disconnected from the server." Locally, my app launches perfectly from the RStudio IDE. I checked my shinyapps.io settings, and users should be disconnected after an instance is idle for 12 minutes. Does anyone have an idea what might cause this to prematurely happen? My (somewhat-exotically-themed) app is here.


Thanks so much for any troubleshooting  suggestions.

~Jeremy

Below, I've included log information from deploy window of RStudio and my UI and server code. 


On the RStudio end, the deploy window most recently states:

Preparing to deploy application...DONE
Uploading bundle for application: 83636...DONE
Deploying bundle: 373363 for application: 83636 ...
Waiting for task: 150753993
  building: Parsing manifest
  building: Building image: 367011
  building: Fetching packages
  building: Installing packages
  building: Installing files
  building: Pushing image: 367011
  deploying: Starting instances
  rollforward: Activating new instances
  terminating: Stopping old instances
Application successfully deployed to https://jschwartzbord.shinyapps.io/euro_cheese/
Deployment completed: https://jschwartzbord.shinyapps.io/euro_cheese/

############################
#ui.R


library(leaflet)
library(shiny)
#EU Countries with codes
shinyUI(fluidPage(
  eu_countries <- read.csv("data/eu_countries.csv", header=T, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  ,
  titlePanel("Euro Cheese"),
  
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      img(src = "R_logo.png", 
          height = 35, width = 35),
          code("made by JRS with Shiny in ", 
          span("RStudio", style = "color:blue"))
    ),
    mainPanel(
      "These data are available from ", a("Eurostat",link = "http://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/products-datasets/-/tag00040"),", which features figures that you can compare to those here.",
      h3("Germany, France, Italy, and Poland take the lead with Europe's cheese production!"),
      leafletOutput("map", width = "100%"),
      p(),
      "*Circle areas proportionate to production of cheese among EU countries in 2014",
      br(),
      br(),
      p("Lucky for us, Eurostat started keeping tabs on EU cheese production beginning in 2003. Which countries have seen production soar since 2003? Which have stagnated? Check out longitudinal EU cheese data below by selecting a country:"),
      selectInput("country", label = h4("Country"), 
                  choices = (eu_countries), selected = "France"),
      plotOutput("plot", width = "100%"),
      p("Keep in mind that these data are expressed in 1000 metric tons (i.e., Italy, France, and Germany produced over one million metric tons of cheese in 2013. Consider that the US dairy sector produced",  a("5,034,875 metric tons", link= "http://www.idfa.org/news-views/media-kits/cheese/cheese-production"), "of cheese in 2013, but that certainly was not all brie and mozarella di bufala.(Twenty-nine percent of US production in 2013 was cheddar.) Below, find  data on national european cheese imports to the US."),
      h3("USA Imports of Cheese from EU Countries"),
      selectInput("year", label =h3("Choose a year:"),
                  choices = 2003:2014, selected = "2003"),
#      checkboxGroupInput("countryGroup", label = "Country", choices = list("France","Germany"),selected = "France"
#                      ),
      plotOutput("fas_plot", width = "175%"),
      p("Looks like Americans are consuming a small proverbial wedge of European cheese. To help Europe, by its cheese!"),
      p("Data obtained from", a("USDA Foreign Agriculture Service (FAS U.S. Trade, Imports - Consumption, accessed February 2016)", link = "http://apps.fas.usda.gov/gats/default.aspx"))
      )
    )
  )
)

############################
#server 
#load data
#eurostat cheese data
setwd("~/Documents/Shiny/euro_cheese")
euro_cheese <- read.table(file = "data/euro_cheese.csv",
                          header = T, 
                          sep = ",", 
                          stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

#USA import data from the USDA Foreign Ag Service
fas <- read.csv("data/fas_cheese.csv",
                stringsAsFactors = FALSE, 
                header =T,
                dec = ".")

convert <- function(x){ as.numeric(gsub(pattern = ",",replacement = "",x))}
fas2 <- data.frame(fas[,1],apply(fas[,c(2:13)], 2, FUN = convert))
#Convert data to be in 1000 metric tons
fas2 <- data.frame(fas2[1],fas2[,-1]/1000)

#libraries
library(devtools)
library(leaflet)
library(ggmap)
library(ggplot2)
library(reshape)

shinyServer(
  function(input, output) {
    output$map <- renderLeaflet({
      
      leaflet(euro_cheese) %>%
      setView(lng=14.550072, lat= 47, zoom = 4) %>%
      addTiles() %>% 
      addCircleMarkers(~lon, ~lat,radius =~0.01*( euro_cheese$X2014))
        
      #add key indicating data correspond to 2014
      #include popup to indicate total production and country per bubble
          })
    output$plot <- renderPlot({
      y <- melt(euro_cheese[match(input$country, euro_cheese$country), 3:13],)
      y$variable <- gsub("X", "", y$variable)
      y$variable <- as.integer(as.character(y$variable))
      qplot(y$variable,y$value, ylab = "Total Cheese Production (1000 tons)", xlab = "Year", main = input$country, geom = "line" )
    })
    output$fas_plot <- renderPlot({
      data <- switch(input$year,
                     "2003" = fas2$X2003,
                     "2004" = fas2$X2004,
                     "2005" = fas2$X2005,
                     "2006" = fas2$X2006,
                     "2007" = fas2$X2007,
                     "2008" = fas2$X2008,
                     "2009" = fas2$X2009,
                     "2010" = fas2$X2010,
                     "2011" = fas2$X2011,
                     "2012" = fas2$X2012,
                     "2013" = fas2$X2013,
                     "2014" = fas2$X2005,)
      qplot(x = fas2$fas...1., y= data, xlab = "Country",
            ylab= "1000 Tons of Cheese Imports"
            )
    })
})

parts:
Hi Hannah
For shinyapps.io related issues, you will want to post it to the shinyapps-users discussion list: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/shinyapps-users

I would encourage you to take a look at the logs from your application as Andy mentioned to see if the error is apparent.  If possible, I would also include a link to your application in case it is easy to spot a javascript issue you may be having.

-Tareef
